title: Attention Mechanisms
description: Attention mechanisms: Neural networks'te önemli bilgiye focus. Self-attention, multi-head attention, cross-attention. Transformers'ın temeli (BERT, GPT, Vision Transformers). Seq2seq, NLP, computer vision.

content.level0_basic: Attention Mechanism, model'in input'un hangi kısmına focus edeceğini dinamik olarak öğrenmesini sağlar. RNN/LSTM'de problem: Uzun sequence'lerde information bottleneck (tüm bilgi son hidden state'te). Attention çözümü: Her time step'e doğrudan erişim, weighted sum (önemli parts'a daha fazla weight). Örnek: Machine translation 'The cat sat on the mat' → 'Le chat'. 'cat' translate ederken source'ta 'cat'e attention verir. Query-Key-Value paradigm: Query (ne arıyorum?), Key (ne var?), Value (içerik). Attention score = similarity(Query, Key), output = weighted sum of Values.
content.level1_beginner: Attention türleri: (1) **Additive Attention (Bahdanau)**: score = v^T·tanh(W_q·Q + W_k·K). Neural network ile similarity. (2) **Multiplicative Attention (Luong)**: score = Q·K^T. Dot product, daha hızlı. (3) **Scaled Dot-Product**: score = (Q·K^T)/√d_k. Scale factor (stability). (4) **Self-Attention**: Query=Key=Value=input. Sequence içi relationships (her token diğerlerine attend eder). (5) **Multi-Head Attention**: Parallel attention'lar (8-16 heads). Farklı representation subspaces. (6) **Cross-Attention**: Query≠Key/Value. Encoder-decoder (decoder encoder'a attend eder). Softmax → attention weights (sum=1). Output = Σ(weight_i · value_i). Transformers: Self-attention + position encoding + feedforward → state-of-the-art NLP.
content.level2_application: Pratik uygulamalar: (1) **Machine Translation**: Seq2seq + attention. Encoder (source) → decoder (target), cross-attention (decoder encoder'a bakar). BLEU score improvement %10-20. (2) **Text Summarization**: Self-attention (long document), cross-attention (summary → source). BERT, T5. (3) **Question Answering**: Query (question), Key/Value (context). Cross-attention, answer span extraction. (4) **Image Captioning**: Vision encoder (CNN/ViT) → text decoder. Cross-attention (decoder image features'a attend). (5) **Vision Transformers (ViT)**: Image patches → self-attention. No convolution, pure attention. ImageNet SOTA. (6) **Speech Recognition**: Audio frames → self-attention → text. Wav2Vec 2.0, Whisper. (7) **Recommendation**: User-item interaction, self-attention (sequence modeling). Next item prediction. Framework'ler: PyTorch (nn.MultiheadAttention), Transformers (Hugging Face), JAX (Flax).
content.level3_advanced: İleri seviye: (1) **Positional Encoding**: Self-attention position-agnostic. Solution: Sinusoidal encoding, learned embeddings. PE(pos, 2i) = sin(pos/10000^(2i/d)), PE(pos, 2i+1) = cos. Relative position (Transformer-XL, T5). (2) **Masking**: (a) Padding mask (variable length). (b) Causal mask (autoregressive, GPT-style, no future leakage). (c) Attention mask (custom patterns). (3) **Efficient Attention**: (a) Sparse attention (Sparse Transformer, local+strided). (b) Linformer (low-rank projection, O(N)). (c) Performer (kernel approximation, O(N)). (d) Flash Attention (IO-aware, GPU memory efficient). (4) **Relative Position**: T5, Transformer-XL. Bias term: score += relative_position_bias(i-j). Better extrapolation (longer sequences). (5) **Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE)**: LLaMA, GPT-NeoX. Rotation matrix, multiplicative. Length extrapolation. (6) **Cross-Attention Variants**: (a) Co-attention (both directions). (b) Bidirectional cross-attention. (c) Memory-augmented (external memory). (7) **Layer Normalization**: Pre-norm vs post-norm. Pre-norm (GPT-3, stability), post-norm (original Transformer).
content.level4_expert: Expert seviyede, architecture variants, optimization ve research frontiers önemlidir. (1) **Architecture Variants**: (a) Encoder-only (BERT, RoBERTa) - bidirectional, classification/understanding. (b) Decoder-only (GPT, LLaMA) - autoregressive, generation. (c) Encoder-decoder (T5, BART) - seq2seq. (2) **Optimization**: (a) Flash Attention (IO-aware, 2-4x faster, memory efficient). (b) Multi-query attention (shared Key/Value, faster inference). (c) Grouped-query attention (LLaMA 2, middle ground). (d) KV cache (inference, cache Key/Value, avoid recomputation). (3) **Long Context**: (a) Sparse attention (local + global). (b) Sliding window (Longformer, 4K-16K tokens). (c) Recurrence (Transformer-XL, segment-level). (d) Compression (Compressive Transformer, memory compression). (e) Retrieval-augmented (RAG, external memory). (4) **Vision**: (a) ViT (patch-based, 16x16 patches). (b) Swin Transformer (hierarchical, shifted windows). (c) DETR (object detection, set prediction). (d) Mask2Former (segmentation). (5) **Cross-Modal**: (a) CLIP (image-text, contrastive). (b) Flamingo (vision-language, few-shot). (c) Perceiver (arbitrary modalities, cross-attention to latents). (6) **Training Stability**: (a) Warm-up (learning rate). (b) Gradient clipping. (c) Pre-norm (layer norm before attention). (d) Weight initialization (Xavier, He). Research: **Mixture of Experts** (MoE, conditional computation), **State Space Models** (Mamba, sub-quadratic), **Hyena** (convolution-based, no attention), **RetNet** (retention, linear complexity).

whatIsIt: Attention Mechanism: Weighted sum of values, weights = similarity(query, keys). Matematiksel: Attention(Q,K,V) = softmax((Q·K^T)/√d_k)·V. Query (d_q), Key (d_k), Value (d_v). Score = Q·K^T (dot product), scale by √d_k (stability), softmax (normalize), multiply by V. Multi-head: Parallel attention (h heads), concat, project. Self-attention: Q=K=V=input. Cross-attention: Q≠K=V. Complexity: O(N²·D) (N=sequence length, D=dimension). Memory: O(N²) attention matrix.
whyNeeded: Attention kritik çünkü: (1) **Long-Range Dependencies**: RNN/LSTM'de vanishing gradient, information bottleneck. Attention: Direct connection, path length O(1). (2) **Parallelization**: RNN sequential (t_i depends t_{i-1}). Attention: Paralel computation (all positions simultaneously). Training 10-100x faster. (3) **Interpretability**: Attention weights görselleştirilebilir. Model hangi input'a focus ediyor? Explainability. (4) **SOTA Performance**: Transformers NLP'de dominant (BERT, GPT-4, T5). Vision (ViT, Swin). Speech (Whisper). (5) **Flexibility**: Seq2seq, classification, generation, multi-modal. Architecture versatile. (6) **Transfer Learning**: Pre-training (BERT/GPT) → fine-tuning. Few-shot, zero-shot (GPT-3/4). Foundation models. (7) **Scale**: Attention scales with model size. GPT-4 (1.7T parameters), LLaMA (70B). Emergent abilities (reasoning, math).
realWorldAnalogy: Attention'ı bir konferansta not almaya benzetebiliriz. **Durum**: 3 saatlik konferans (long sequence), her şeyi ezberleyemezsin (information bottleneck). **RNN yaklaşımı**: Her cümleyi dinle, önceki not'a ekle → son not tüm bilgiyi içermeli (impossible, 3 saat sıkıştır!). **Attention yaklaşımı**: (1) **Query**: 'ML optimization nedir?' diye soruyorsun (ne arıyorum?). (2) **Keys**: Konferans tüm slides (available information). (3) **Similarity**: Her slide'a bak, query ile ilgili mi? 'Optimization' keyword içeren slides → high score. (4) **Attention Weights**: İlgili slides'lara %80 attention, irrelevant'lara %20. (5) **Values**: İlgili slides'ın içeriğini weighted sum → cevap. **Multi-Head**: 8 farklı kişi 8 farklı soru soruyor (farklı perspectives). Bir kişi 'optimization', diğeri 'deep learning', diğeri 'applications'. Her head farklı aspect'e focus → birleştir → comprehensive understanding. **Self-Attention**: Slides arası relationships (slide 5 slide 2'ye refer eder). **Cross-Attention**: Soru-cevap (question → slides).

formulas: \text{Scaled Dot-Product Attention}: \quad \text{Attention}(Q, K, V) = \text{softmax}\left(\frac{Q K^T}{\sqrt{d_k}}\right) V
\text{Multi-Head Attention}: \quad \text{MultiHead}(Q,K,V) = \text{Concat}(\text{head}_1, ..., \text{head}_h) W^O \quad \text{where } \text{head}_i = \text{Attention}(Q W_i^Q, K W_i^K, V W_i^V)
\text{Additive Attention (Bahdanau)}: \quad s_{ij} = v^T \tanh(W_q q_i + W_k k_j) \quad \text{(neural network scoring)}

stepByStep: 1. **Input Preparation**: Input sequence X ∈ R^(N×D). Embedding layer (tokens → vectors). Add positional encoding (position information). Result: X' = Embedding(X) + PE.
2. **Linear Projections**: Query, Key, Value projections. Q = X'·W_Q (N×d_q), K = X'·W_K (N×d_k), V = X'·W_V (N×d_v). Typically d_q = d_k = d_v = d_model/h (h=num heads).
3. **Compute Scores**: Attention scores = Q·K^T (N×N matrix). Each element s_ij = q_i·k_j (dot product, measures similarity). Scale: scores / √d_k (prevent large values, softmax stability).

4. **Apply Mask (optional)**: (a) Padding mask: Mask padding tokens (set score = -inf → softmax = 0). (b) Causal mask: Autoregressive (GPT), mask future positions (lower triangular). (c) Custom mask: Application-specific.
5. **Softmax**: Attention weights α = softmax(scores). Each row sums to 1 (probability distribution). α_ij = exp(s_ij) / Σ_k exp(s_ik). High score → high weight.
6. **Weighted Sum**: Output O = α·V (N×d_v). Each output vector o_i = Σ_j α_ij·v_j (weighted average of values). Attended representation.
7. **Multi-Head (if applicable)**: Repeat steps 2-6 for h heads (parallel). Each head: different W_Q, W_K, W_V. Concat outputs (N×(h·d_v)), project: O_final = Concat(head_1,...,head_h)·W_O.
8. **Residual Connection**: Output + input (X' + O_final). Skip connection, gradient flow. Prevents vanishing gradients in deep networks.
9. **Layer Normalization**: LayerNorm(X' + O_final). Normalize across feature dimension (mean=0, std=1). Stabilizes training. Pre-norm (modern) vs post-norm (original).
10. **Feedforward Network**: MLP(LayerNorm(X' + O_final)). Two linear layers + activation (ReLU, GELU). Expand (4x), compress. Residual + LayerNorm. Complete Transformer block.
algorithm.complexity: **Zaman Karmaşıklığı**: Attention: O(N²·D) (N=seq length, D=model dimension). Q·K^T: O(N²·D), softmax: O(N²), α·V: O(N²·D). Multi-head (h heads): O(h·N²·D) = O(N²·D) (typically D_total = h·d_head). **Uzay**: Attention matrix: O(N²) (dominant for long sequences). KV cache (inference): O(N·D) per layer. Model parameters: O(D²) (projection matrices). **Efficient Variants**: Sparse attention: O(N·√N) or O(N·log N), Linformer: O(N·D), Performer/Flash: O(N·D). **Parallelization**: Fully parallel (all positions simultaneously), unlike RNN O(N) sequential. Training: 10-100x faster. **Inference**: O(N²·D) per token (autoregressive). KV cache: avoid recomputation. Batch processing: throughput ↑.

codeExamples.title: Scaled Dot-Product Attention (NumPy)
codeExamples.code:
import numpy as np

def scaled_dot_product_attention(Q, K, V, mask=None):
    """
    Q: Query (batch, seq_len, d_k)
    K: Key (batch, seq_len, d_k)
    V: Value (batch, seq_len, d_v)
    mask: Optional mask (batch, seq_len, seq_len)
    """
    d_k = Q.shape[-1]
    
    # Compute attention scores
    scores = np.matmul(Q, K.transpose(0, 2, 1)) / np.sqrt(d_k)
    print(f'Scores shape: {scores.shape}')
    print(f'Scores (before softmax):\n{scores[0, 0, :5]}')  # First 5
    
    # Apply mask (if provided)
    if mask is not None:
        scores = np.where(mask == 0, -1e9, scores)
    
    # Softmax
    attention_weights = np.exp(scores - np.max(scores, axis=-1, keepdims=True))
    attention_weights = attention_weights / np.sum(attention_weights, axis=-1, keepdims=True)
    
    print(f'\nAttention weights (after softmax):\n{attention_weights[0, 0, :5]}')
    print(f'Sum: {attention_weights[0, 0].sum():.4f} (should be 1.0)')
    
    # Weighted sum
    output = np.matmul(attention_weights, V)
    
    return output, attention_weights

# Example
batch_size = 1
seq_len = 8
d_k = 64
d_v = 64

np.random.seed(42)
Q = np.random.randn(batch_size, seq_len, d_k)
K = np.random.randn(batch_size, seq_len, d_k)
V = np.random.randn(batch_size, seq_len, d_v)

print('=== Scaled Dot-Product Attention ===')
print(f'Input shapes: Q={Q.shape}, K={K.shape}, V={V.shape}')

output, weights = scaled_dot_product_attention(Q, K, V)

print(f'\nOutput shape: {output.shape}')
print('\nAttention mechanism: weighted sum of Values based on Query-Key similarity')
codeExamples.explanation: Scaled dot-product attention: Core mechanism. Q·K^T (similarity), scale by √d_k, softmax (weights), multiply by V. Numpy implementation.

codeExamples.title: Multi-Head Attention (PyTorch)
codeExamples.code:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

class MultiHeadAttention(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, d_model=512, num_heads=8):
        super().__init__()
        assert d_model % num_heads == 0, 'd_model must be divisible by num_heads'
        
        self.d_model = d_model
        self.num_heads = num_heads
        self.d_k = d_model // num_heads
        
        # Linear projections
        self.W_q = nn.Linear(d_model, d_model)
        self.W_k = nn.Linear(d_model, d_model)
        self.W_v = nn.Linear(d_model, d_model)
        self.W_o = nn.Linear(d_model, d_model)
    
    def split_heads(self, x, batch_size):
        """Split last dimension into (num_heads, d_k)"""
        x = x.view(batch_size, -1, self.num_heads, self.d_k)
        return x.transpose(1, 2)  # (batch, num_heads, seq_len, d_k)
    
    def forward(self, Q, K, V, mask=None):
        batch_size = Q.size(0)
        
        # Linear projections
        Q = self.W_q(Q)  # (batch, seq_len, d_model)
        K = self.W_k(K)
        V = self.W_v(V)
        
        # Split into multiple heads
        Q = self.split_heads(Q, batch_size)  # (batch, num_heads, seq_len, d_k)
        K = self.split_heads(K, batch_size)
        V = self.split_heads(V, batch_size)
        
        # Scaled dot-product attention
        scores = torch.matmul(Q, K.transpose(-2, -1)) / torch.sqrt(torch.tensor(self.d_k, dtype=torch.float32))
        
        if mask is not None:
            scores = scores.masked_fill(mask == 0, -1e9)
        
        attention_weights = F.softmax(scores, dim=-1)
        output = torch.matmul(attention_weights, V)  # (batch, num_heads, seq_len, d_k)
        
        # Concat heads
        output = output.transpose(1, 2).contiguous().view(batch_size, -1, self.d_model)
        
        # Final projection
        output = self.W_o(output)
        
        return output, attention_weights

# Example
d_model = 512
num_heads = 8
seq_len = 10
batch_size = 2

X = torch.randn(batch_size, seq_len, d_model)

mha = MultiHeadAttention(d_model, num_heads)
output, weights = mha(X, X, X)  # Self-attention

print(f'Input shape: {X.shape}')
print(f'Output shape: {output.shape}')
print(f'Attention weights shape: {weights.shape}')  # (batch, num_heads, seq_len, seq_len)
print(f'\nNum parameters: {sum(p.numel() for p in mha.parameters()):,}')
print('\nMulti-head attention: 8 parallel attention mechanisms, different perspectives')
codeExamples.explanation: Multi-head attention: h parallel attentions (8 heads typical). Farklı representation subspaces. Concat + project. Transformers'ın core component.

codeExamples.title: Self-Attention with Masking
codeExamples.code:
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

def self_attention(X, mask_type='none'):
    """
    X: Input (batch, seq_len, d_model)
    mask_type: 'none', 'causal', or 'padding'
    """
    batch_size, seq_len, d_model = X.shape
    
    # Simple projection (for demo, use X directly as Q, K, V)
    Q = K = V = X
    
    # Scores
    d_k = d_model
    scores = torch.matmul(Q, K.transpose(-2, -1)) / torch.sqrt(torch.tensor(d_k, dtype=torch.float32))
    
    # Apply mask
    if mask_type == 'causal':
        # Autoregressive: no future information
        mask = torch.tril(torch.ones(seq_len, seq_len))
        scores = scores.masked_fill(mask == 0, -1e9)
        print('Causal mask applied (lower triangular)')
    elif mask_type == 'padding':
        # Padding mask (last 3 positions are padding)
        padding_mask = torch.ones(batch_size, seq_len)
        padding_mask[:, -3:] = 0  # Last 3 tokens are padding
        padding_mask = padding_mask.unsqueeze(1).unsqueeze(2)  # (batch, 1, 1, seq_len)
        scores = scores.masked_fill(padding_mask == 0, -1e9)
        print('Padding mask applied (last 3 positions)')
    
    # Softmax
    attention_weights = F.softmax(scores, dim=-1)
    
    # Output
    output = torch.matmul(attention_weights, V)
    
    return output, attention_weights

# Example
torch.manual_seed(42)
seq_len = 8
d_model = 64
X = torch.randn(1, seq_len, d_model)

print('=== Self-Attention with Different Masks ===\n')

# No mask
output_none, weights_none = self_attention(X, mask_type='none')
print(f'No mask - Attention weights shape: {weights_none.shape}')

# Causal mask (GPT-style)
output_causal, weights_causal = self_attention(X, mask_type='causal')

# Padding mask
output_padding, weights_padding = self_attention(X, mask_type='padding')

# Visualize
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(15, 4))

for ax, weights, title in zip(axes, 
                               [weights_none[0,0], weights_causal[0,0], weights_padding[0,0]],
                               ['No Mask', 'Causal Mask', 'Padding Mask']):
    im = ax.imshow(weights.detach().numpy(), cmap='viridis')
    ax.set_title(title)
    ax.set_xlabel('Key position')
    ax.set_ylabel('Query position')
    plt.colorbar(im, ax=ax)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

print('\nCausal mask: Autoregressive (GPT), no future info')
print('Padding mask: Ignore padding tokens')
codeExamples.explanation: Masking: Causal (autoregressive, GPT), Padding (variable length), Custom. Mask score → -inf, softmax → 0. Critical for different tasks.

codeExamples.title: Positional Encoding
codeExamples.code:
import torch
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

def positional_encoding(seq_len, d_model):
    """
    Sinusoidal positional encoding
    PE(pos, 2i) = sin(pos / 10000^(2i/d_model))
    PE(pos, 2i+1) = cos(pos / 10000^(2i/d_model))
    """
    position = torch.arange(seq_len).unsqueeze(1)  # (seq_len, 1)
    div_term = torch.exp(torch.arange(0, d_model, 2) * -(np.log(10000.0) / d_model))
    
    pe = torch.zeros(seq_len, d_model)
    pe[:, 0::2] = torch.sin(position * div_term)
    pe[:, 1::2] = torch.cos(position * div_term)
    
    return pe

# Generate
seq_len = 100
d_model = 128

pe = positional_encoding(seq_len, d_model)

print(f'Positional encoding shape: {pe.shape}')
print(f'First position encoding (first 10 dims):\n{pe[0, :10]}')
print(f'\nSecond position encoding (first 10 dims):\n{pe[1, :10]}')

# Visualize
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))

plt.subplot(1, 2, 1)
plt.imshow(pe.T.numpy(), aspect='auto', cmap='coolwarm')
plt.xlabel('Position')
plt.ylabel('Dimension')
plt.title('Positional Encoding Heatmap')
plt.colorbar()

plt.subplot(1, 2, 2)
for i in range(0, d_model, 16):
    plt.plot(pe[:, i].numpy(), label=f'dim {i}')
plt.xlabel('Position')
plt.ylabel('Value')
plt.title('PE Values Over Position')
plt.legend()
plt.grid(alpha=0.3)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

print('\nPositional encoding: Inject position information')
print('Sinusoidal: Different frequencies, learns relative positions')
print('Usage: X_input = Embedding(tokens) + PE')
codeExamples.explanation: Positional Encoding: Self-attention position-agnostic. Sinusoidal encoding (sin/cos, different frequencies). Add to embeddings. Relative position learning.

codeExamples.title: Attention Visualization
codeExamples.code:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

# Simple attention model
class SimpleAttention(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, d_model=64):
        super().__init__()
        self.W_q = nn.Linear(d_model, d_model)
        self.W_k = nn.Linear(d_model, d_model)
        self.W_v = nn.Linear(d_model, d_model)
        self.d_k = d_model
    
    def forward(self, X):
        Q = self.W_q(X)
        K = self.W_k(X)
        V = self.W_v(X)
        
        scores = torch.matmul(Q, K.transpose(-2, -1)) / np.sqrt(self.d_k)
        attention_weights = torch.softmax(scores, dim=-1)
        output = torch.matmul(attention_weights, V)
        
        return output, attention_weights

# Example sentence
sentence = ['The', 'cat', 'sat', 'on', 'the', 'mat']
seq_len = len(sentence)
d_model = 64

# Random embeddings (in practice: learned embeddings)
torch.manual_seed(42)
X = torch.randn(1, seq_len, d_model)

# Model
model = SimpleAttention(d_model)
output, attention_weights = model(X)

print(f'Sentence: {" ".join(sentence)}')
print(f'\nAttention weights shape: {attention_weights.shape}')

# Visualize
weights = attention_weights[0].detach().numpy()

plt.figure(figsize=(8, 6))
plt.imshow(weights, cmap='Blues')
plt.xticks(range(seq_len), sentence)
plt.yticks(range(seq_len), sentence)
plt.xlabel('Key (attending to)')
plt.ylabel('Query (from)')
plt.title('Self-Attention Weights Visualization')
plt.colorbar(label='Attention Weight')

# Add text annotations
for i in range(seq_len):
    for j in range(seq_len):
        plt.text(j, i, f'{weights[i, j]:.2f}', 
                ha='center', va='center', 
                color='white' if weights[i, j] > 0.5 else 'black',
                fontsize=8)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

print('\nInterpretation: Each row shows what that token attends to')
print('Example: "cat" might attend strongly to "The" and "sat"')
print('Diagonal: Self-attention (token to itself)')

codeExamples.title: Efficient Attention: Flash Attention Concept
codeExamples.code:
import torch
import time

def standard_attention(Q, K, V):
    """Standard attention: materializes N x N attention matrix"""
    d_k = Q.size(-1)
    scores = torch.matmul(Q, K.transpose(-2, -1)) / (d_k ** 0.5)
    attention = torch.softmax(scores, dim=-1)
    output = torch.matmul(attention, V)
    return output

def flash_attention_concept(Q, K, V, block_size=256):
    """
    Flash Attention concept: Block-wise computation
    Reduces memory from O(N^2) to O(N)
    In practice: use official FlashAttention implementation
    """
    batch_size, seq_len, d_k = Q.shape
    output = torch.zeros_like(Q)
    
    # Process in blocks (simplified, not actual Flash Attention)
    num_blocks = (seq_len + block_size - 1) // block_size
    
    for i in range(num_blocks):
        start_i = i * block_size
        end_i = min((i + 1) * block_size, seq_len)
        Q_block = Q[:, start_i:end_i, :]
        
        for j in range(num_blocks):
            start_j = j * block_size
            end_j = min((j + 1) * block_size, seq_len)
            K_block = K[:, start_j:end_j, :]
            V_block = V[:, start_j:end_j, :]
            
            # Block attention
            scores = torch.matmul(Q_block, K_block.transpose(-2, -1)) / (d_k ** 0.5)
            attention = torch.softmax(scores, dim=-1)
            output[:, start_i:end_i, :] += torch.matmul(attention, V_block)
    
    return output

# Benchmark
seq_len = 1024
d_model = 64
batch_size = 1

Q = torch.randn(batch_size, seq_len, d_model)
K = torch.randn(batch_size, seq_len, d_model)
V = torch.randn(batch_size, seq_len, d_model)

print(f'Sequence length: {seq_len}, d_model: {d_model}')
print(f'Attention matrix size: {seq_len}x{seq_len} = {seq_len**2:,} elements')
print(f'Memory: {seq_len**2 * 4 / 1e6:.2f} MB (FP32)\n')

# Standard attention
start = time.time()
output_std = standard_attention(Q, K, V)
std_time = time.time() - start

# Flash attention (concept)
start = time.time()
output_flash = flash_attention_concept(Q, K, V, block_size=256)
flash_time = time.time() - start

print(f'Standard attention: {std_time*1000:.2f} ms')
print(f'Flash attention (concept): {flash_time*1000:.2f} ms')

print('\n=== Flash Attention Benefits ===')
print('1. Memory: O(N^2) → O(N) (block-wise)')
print('2. Speed: 2-4x faster (IO-aware, GPU memory hierarchy)')
print('3. Exact: Same output as standard attention')
print('4. Long sequences: Enables 16K-100K tokens')
print('\nUse: pip install flash-attn (official implementation)')
codeExamples.explanation: Flash Attention: IO-aware, block-wise computation. Memory O(N²)→O(N), 2-4x faster. Critical for long sequences (16K-100K tokens). GPU memory efficient.

quiz.question: Attention mechanism'in temel prensibi nedir?
options: Weighted sum of values, weights = similarity(query, keys). Önemli bilgiye focus
quiz.explanation: Attention: Query-Key similarity → weights (softmax), weighted sum of Values. Dinamik focus (önemli bilgi >> weight). RNN bottleneck çözümü.

quiz.question: Self-attention vs cross-attention farkı?
options: Self-attention: Q=K=V=input (sequence içi). Cross-attention: Q≠K=V (iki farklı sequence)
quiz.explanation: Self-attention: Sequence içi relationships (Q=K=V). Cross-attention: İki sequence arası (örn: decoder → encoder, Q≠K=V). Seq2seq'te critical.

quiz.question: Multi-head attention neden kullanılır?
options: Farklı representation subspaces (8-16 heads). Her head farklı aspect'e focus. Parallel attention
quiz.explanation: Multi-head: h parallel attention (8 heads typical). Farklı perspectives (syntax, semantics, etc.). Concat + project. Richer representation.

quiz.question: Scaled dot-product'ta √d_k neden kullanılır?
options: Softmax stability. Büyük d_k → large dot products → softmax saturates (gradient ≈0). Scale prevents
quiz.explanation: Scale by √d_k: Dot product variance = d_k. √d_k ile normalize → variance=1. Softmax stability (no saturation), gradient flow better.

quiz.question: Positional encoding neden gerekli?
options: Self-attention position-agnostic (permutation invariant). PE inject position info. Sinusoidal: relative position
quiz.explanation: Self-attention position-agnostic (order bilmiyor). PE ekle: Sinusoidal (sin/cos, different frequencies) veya learned. Relative position learning.

quiz.question: Causal masking ne için kullanılır?
options: Autoregressive models (GPT). No future information leak. Lower triangular mask (position i sadece ≤i'ye attend)
quiz.explanation: Causal mask: Autoregressive (GPT, language generation). Position i sadece ≤i'ye attend (no future). Lower triangular. Training/inference consistent.

quiz.question: Attention complexity nedir?
options: O(N²·D). N=seq length, D=dimension. Attention matrix N×N. Bottleneck for long sequences
quiz.explanation: Complexity: O(N²·D). Q·K^T: O(N²·D), softmax: O(N²), α·V: O(N²·D). Memory: O(N²) attention matrix. Long seq problem (16K tokens → 256M elements).

quiz.question: Flash Attention'ın avantajı nedir?
options: IO-aware, block-wise. Memory O(N²)→O(N), 2-4x faster. Long sequences (16K-100K tokens) enable
quiz.explanation: Flash Attention: Block-wise computation, IO-aware (GPU memory hierarchy). Memory O(N²)→O(N), 2-4x speedup. Long context (16K+ tokens). Exact output.

flashcards.back: Weighted sum: Attention(Q,K,V) = softmax((Q·K^T)/√d_k)·V. Query-Key similarity → weights, weighted sum of Values. Dynamic focus.
Q=K=V=input. Sequence içi relationships. Her token diğerlerine attend. Transformers core. Position-agnostic (PE gerekir).
h parallel attention (8 heads). Farklı W_Q, W_K, W_V. Farklı subspaces (syntax, semantics). Concat + project. Richer representation.
Q≠K=V. İki sequence arası. Decoder → Encoder (seq2seq). Image captioning (text → image features). Query from one, Key/Value from another.
Score = (Q·K^T)/√d_k. Scale factor: softmax stability (prevent saturation). √d_k: normalize variance. Softmax → weights.
Inject position info. Sinusoidal: PE(pos,2i)=sin(pos/10000^(2i/d)), PE(pos,2i+1)=cos. Learned embeddings alternative. Relative position.
Autoregressive (GPT). No future leak. Lower triangular mask (position i → ≤i). Score → -inf, softmax → 0. Training/inference consistent.
O(N²·D). N=seq length, D=dimension. Attention matrix N×N (memory O(N²)). Long sequences problem. Efficient: Sparse, Linformer, Flash.
IO-aware, block-wise. Memory O(N²)→O(N), 2-4x faster. GPU memory efficient. Long context (16K-100K tokens). Exact output.
Inference optimization. Cache Key/Value (autoregressive). Avoid recomputation. Memory: O(N·D) per layer. Faster generation.
O(N²) → O(N·√N) or O(N·log N). Local + strided (Sparse Transformer), sliding window (Longformer). Long sequences (4K-16K).
Q: ne arıyorum? K: ne var? V: içerik. Similarity(Q,K) → weights. Weighted sum(V) → output. Information retrieval paradigm.

commonMistakes.why: Self-attention position-agnostic (permutation invariant). PE olmadan: 'cat sat' = 'sat cat'. Order bilgisi kaybolur. NLP/seq tasks fail.
commonMistakes.fix: PE ekle: Sinusoidal (Transformer original), learned embeddings (BERT), relative position (T5, Transformer-XL). X_input = Embedding + PE. Always!

commonMistakes.why: GPT-style models: Training'de future bilgisi leak olur (cheating). Test'te olmaz → train/test mismatch. Model fail.
commonMistakes.fix: Causal mask: Lower triangular (position i → ≤i). Training/inference both. mask = torch.tril(torch.ones(N,N)). scores.masked_fill(mask==0, -inf).

commonMistakes.why: Büyük d_k (512, 1024): Dot product variance ↑ (∝ d_k). Softmax saturates (one hot), gradients ≈0. Training instability.
commonMistakes.fix: Scale: scores / √d_k. Variance normalize (→1). Softmax stable, gradients flow. Standard practice (Transformer paper).

commonMistakes.why: O(N²) memory. 16K tokens → 256M elements (1GB FP32!). OOM (out of memory). GPU memory limited.
commonMistakes.fix: Efficient attention: Flash Attention (block-wise, O(N)), Sparse (local+strided), Linformer (low-rank), Performer (kernel). Or: chunk sequences.

commonMistakes.why: Single head: Tek perspective. Çeşitli linguistic phenomena capture edemez (syntax, semantics, coreference). Expressiveness limited.
commonMistakes.fix: Multi-head (8-16 heads typical). Farklı subspaces, richer representation. Concat + project. BERT (12 heads), GPT-3 (96 heads). Standard.

commonMistakes.why: Autoregressive inference: Her token generation'da tüm sequence recompute (redundant). O(N²·D·L) (L=layers). Slow (GPT-3: 175B params).
commonMistakes.fix: KV cache: Key/Value'ları cache et (reuse). Sadece yeni token compute. O(N·D·L) → O(D·L). 10-100x faster inference. HuggingFace Transformers default.

commonMistakes.why: Variable length sequences: Padding tokens (0 veya [PAD]). Attention padding'e de attend eder (meaningless). Noise, accuracy ↓.
commonMistakes.fix: Padding mask: Padding positions → score = -inf, softmax = 0. No attention to padding. padding_mask = (input == PAD_TOKEN). Critical for batching.
